# Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka (Kd 3)

**ID:** Kd 3
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka* is the third chapter of the Khandhaka section of the Vinaya Piṭaka, situated in the *Mahāvagga* between the *Uposathakkhandhaka* and the *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* [Frauwallner 1956; Norman 1983]. The text prohibits Buddhist monastics from traveling during the three months of the rainy season, instituting the compulsory observance of the rains retreat (*vassa*) in an appropriate residence. The traditional justification for restricting travel during the rains—avoiding injury to small creatures and sprouting plant life—is an ancient Vinaya rationale shared with parallel traditions [Bechert 1992]. Commentarial analysis in the *Samantapāsādikā* observes that within this chapter, the only category of ecclesiastical offence laid down for breaches of its regulations is that of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*) [Horner 1966].

Curated parallels to the *Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka* survive in other early Vinaya lineages under the title *Varṣāvastu*, extant in Sanskrit (Mūlasarvāstivāda), Tibetan, and several Chinese translations of the Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka recensions [Frauwallner 1956; Bechert 1992]. Modern English translations have been produced by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner 1966].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd4 Varsavastu; xct-mu-kd4 Vassa; lzh-mu-kd4 Vassa; Lzh Sarv Kd4 Vassa Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 3 Vassa Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 3 Vassa Khandhaka
- Resembling parallels: Lzh Mg Bu Pn4 Vagga 4. Uposatha

**Sources**

- [Bechert 1992] Heinz Bechert, The Dating of the Historical Buddha, Part 2 (1992) — Discussion of the rationale for vassa rules regarding harming plants and small beings.
- [Bodhi 2009] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination in the Theravāda Tradition (2009) — Details on the allowance to leave the retreat when requested by a sāmaṇerī taking sikkhamānā precepts.
- [Frauwallner 1956] Erich Frauwallner, The Earliest Vinaya and the Beginnings of Buddhist Literature (1956) — Position of the chapter in the Skandhaka structure and its correspondence to the Varṣāvastu.
- [Horner 1966] I. B. Horner, The Book of the Discipline (Vinaya-Piṭaka), Vol. VI (1966) — Commentarial citation from the Samantapāsādikā noting that only dukkaṭa offences occur in Kd 3.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pāli Literature (1983) — Position of the chapter within the Mahāvagga.
